title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook: Process, Runbooks, Postmortems, Rotations, Game Days, and Communication Templates
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview
======
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's standard incident management process, runbook guidelines, postmortem requirements, on-call rotation rules, game day framework, and templates for status page updates and customer communications. It is intended for on-call engineers, incident commanders (ICs), SREs, and engineering managers who participate in incident response and post-incident remediation.

Scope
-----
- Applies to all production-impacting incidents across Redwood-hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Covers detection, alerting, escalation, mitigation, communication, and post-incident follow-up.
- Includes templates and minimum requirements for runbooks, postmortems, and customer-facing messaging.

Goals and Principles
--------------------
- Restore service quickly and safely while preserving evidence for later analysis.
- Communicate early and clearly to internal stakeholders and affected customers.
- Treat incidents as learning opportunities: fix root causes, reduce blast radius, and improve runbooks/SLOs.
- Differentiate communication channels and audiences (internal ops vs. customers vs. executives).

Incident Severity Taxonomy (Severity/Impact)
-------------------------------------------
1) P0 / Sev0 (Critical) \u2013 Systemwide outage 
   - Impact: >50% of traffic, major features unavailable, violated SLA
   - Response time: page immediately, allocate cross-functional incident team
   - Example: cluster control plane down, runaway autoscaler consuming all GPUs
2) P1 / Sev1 (High) \u2013 Significant partial outage
   - Impact: degraded performance for multiple customers or regions, or severe error spikes
   - Response time: page within 5 minutes, on-call lead + product/SRE responders
3) P2 / Sev2 (Moderate) \u2013 Isolated customer or feature degradation
   - Impact: single-customer outage or degraded non-critical functionality
   - Response time: page based on rotation (15\u201360 minutes), follow-up during business hours
4) P3 / Sev3 (Low) \u2013 Informational or scheduled maintenance
   - Impact: minor issues, no customer impact; ticketed for normal triage

Roles & Responsibilities
------------------------
- Pager / Primary Responder: First on-call engineer who investigates alerts and executes runbook steps.
- Incident Commander (IC): Coordinates response, owns communications, tracks timeline and decisions.
- Scribe: Records timeline, actions, commands, and artifacts in the incident log (Confluence incident page).
- Subject Matter Experts (SMEs): Service owners called in as needed (runtime, infra, networking, security).
- Engineering Manager / Escalation Owner: Approves escalations, supports resource allocation and exec comms.

Pager Escalation & Rotation Rules
--------------------------------
- Rotation cadence: 1-week primary rotation, 1-week secondary (fallback) rotation.
- Escalation windows: primary on-call for 8am\u201310pm local region; night/weekend escalation rules documented per-team.
- If pager unanswered for 10 minutes: escalate to secondary; if still unanswered after 15 minutes escalate to on-call manager.
- Contact methods: primary channel is PagerDuty -> Slack -> phone call if severe.

Runbooks: Structure & Minimum Contents
-------------------------------------
Every service runbook must include the following top-level sections:
1. Title and short description
2. Owner and escalation contacts (names, Slack handles, rotation schedule link)
3. Severity mapping and example alerts that should trigger this runbook
4. Preconditions / impact assessment (what to check first)
5. Step-by-step mitigation procedures (numbered)
6. Read-only diagnostics commands and expected output snippets
7. Rollback / safe-state procedures
8. Post-incident actions and runbook maintenance checklist
9. Links to diagrams, dashboards, logs, and tracing (URL strings)

Example Runbook excerpt (Service: inference-api)
------------------------------------------------
1) Confirm alerts: check grafana/influx SLO dashboard -> look for 5m error rate > 3% and P50 latency > 400ms.
2) Identify scope: run query `SELECT count(*) FROM requests WHERE region = 'us-west' AND status >= 500` (example).
3) Check capacity: `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide` and `nvidia-smi` on target hosts.
4) Mitigate: scale down recent canary version, rollback to last known-good model image, or temporarily increase routing weight to fallback region: `redwood ctl traffic set --service inference-api --region us-east --weight 80`
5) Verify: confirm 5m error rate returns to baseline and latencies recover.
6) Declare incident resolved and start postmortem process.

Diagnostic Commands Reference (examples)
--------------------------------------
- kubectl get pods -n inference --selector app=inference-api
- kubectl logs -n inference <pod> --since=10m | tail -n 200
- redwood metrics query --service inference-api --window 5m --metric error_rate
- ssh jumpbox@prod-gpu-01 sudo journalctl -u inference-runtime -n 500

Communication Playbook
----------------------
1) Internal Comms (Slack + Incident Page)
   - Immediately post in #incident-management with short summary: severity, impacted services, initial mitigation, IC, and ETA for next update.
   - Keep cadence: update every 15 minutes for P0/P1 until recovery; every 30\u201360 minutes for P2.
2) External Comms (Status Page & Customers)
   - Status page: publish an initial message within 30 minutes for P0/P1 incidents (see templates below).
   - Customer emails: for targeted customers impacted >30 minutes or any SLA breach, use the customer comms template and route via CS/Account teams.
3) Executive Comms
   - For incidents that may materially impact revenue, major customers, or SLAs, EC must send a concise executive summary within 60\u201390 minutes.

Status Page Templates
---------------------
- Initial (public):
  "Short: Investigating - Increased error rate impacting text generation in US-West.
  Impact: Some customers may see 5xx errors and degraded latency.
  Latest: Engineering investigating; mitigation in progress. Next update: 30 minutes."

- Update (public):
  "Short: Mitigation in progress - Routing traffic away from affected nodes.
  Impact: Partial recovery expected; some requests may still fail.
  Latest: Traffic reroute initiated at 16:30 UTC. Next update: 15 minutes."

- Resolved (public):
  "Short: Resolved - Service restored for all regions.
  Impact: Customers may have experienced intermittent errors between 16:15\u201316:45 UTC.
  Details: Root cause identified as autoscaler configuration regression; rollback performed. Follow-up: Postmortem available in 48 hours."

Customer Communication Templates
-------------------------------
- Short customer email (when small set of customers impacted):
  Subject: Incident affecting inference requests in us-west \u2013 [Resolved/Update]
  Body:
  Hi <Customer name>,

  We experienced an issue impacting inference requests in the us-west region between <start> and <end>. Our team has restored service; the root cause appears to be <brief cause>. We are rolling out a fix and will follow up with a postmortem.

  If you saw persistent errors or data loss, please reply and we will prioritize a remediation plan.

  Regards,
  Redwood Support & Engineering

- Executive customer template (major customers / SLA impact):
  Subject: Incident report \u2013 Service disruption affecting inference throughput
  Body:
  Hello <Customer Exec>,

  Summary: Between <start> and <end> UTC we experienced elevated error rates impacting your inference traffic. Immediate mitigation involved traffic rerouting and a rollback of a recent autoscaler change. We are investigating root cause and expect a full report within 48 hours.

  Next steps: dedicated postmortem with corrective actions, timeline for remediation, and compensation assessment if an SLA was breached.

  Point of contact: <Customer Success Manager name>

Incident Timeline & Postmortem Requirements
-------------------------------------------
- Timeline:
  - Incident declared and IC assigned within 15 minutes for P0/P1.
  - Incident page created in Confluence (use incident-template) and scribe assigned.
  - Postmortem draft due within 72 hours (initial findings) and final postmortem published within 7 calendar days.
- Postmortem must include:
  - Incident summary (what, when, impact), timeline of events, root cause analysis, contributing factors, mitigation performed, customer impact summary, action items (Owner + target date), and lessons learned.
  - All postmortems must have at least one retrospective review meeting (game day or blameless RCA) scheduled within 14 days.

Postmortem Template (minimum fields)
------------------------------------
- Title
- Severity
- Incident lead / scribe
- Start / End timestamps
- Symptoms and detection method
- Root cause
- Sequence of events (annotated timeline)
- Impact summary (customers, SLAs, metrics)
- Short-term mitigations and long-term fixes
- Action items (owner, due date)
- Follow-up: game day schedule, runbook updates, monitoring improvements

Game Days (Exercise and Resilience Testing)
------------------------------------------
- Purpose: validate runbooks, exercise escalation paths, and test cross-team coordination.
- Cadence: quarterly team-level game days; annual company-wide incident simulations.
- Typical scenario: API latency spike with autoscaler regression causing OOM on GPU hosts.
- Roles in game day: IC, scribe, ops, customer comms, executive observer.
- Outcomes: update runbooks, fix gaps in escalation lists, measure MTTR during simulation.

Operational Metrics & SLOs (reference)
------------------------------------
- Latency SLO: P95 generation latency < 350ms for hosted API (target), error rate SLO < 0.5% per 5m window.
- Availability SLO: 99.9% monthly availability for Hosted API.
- MTTR targets: P0 mean time to mitigate (MTTM) < 30 minutes; P1 MTTM < 2 hours.

After-Action and Follow-up
-------------------------
1) Convert postmortem action items into tracked tickets (owner + due date) and add to team roadmap.
2) Update affected runbooks and monitoring alerts within 7 days.
3) Schedule a follow-up review 30 days after incident to confirm remediation completion.

Appendix: Quick reference comms templates (copy/paste)
---------------------------------------------------
- Internal Slack - Initial P0 alert:
  ```
  [P0] Investigating: inference-api errors in us-west. IC: @ava.martinez, Scribe: @diego.rivera. Impact: elevated 5xx rate & latency. Initial mitigation: routing change in progress. Next update in 15m. Incident page: <link>
  ```

- Status page - short initial:
  ```
  Investigating: We are seeing elevated error rates for text generation in US-West. Our engineers are investigating and working on mitigation. Next update in 30 minutes.
  ```

- Public status - resolved:
  ```
  Resolved: Service restored. Affected timeframe: 2026-02-19 16:15\u201316:45 UTC. Root cause: autoscaler misconfiguration introduced in canary. Rollback performed and monitoring validated.
  ```

Ownership & Links
-----------------
- On-call policy owner: eng-sre (pager-ops@redwood.ai)
- Incident templates: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-template
- Runbook index: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks

Maintenance & Review Cycle
--------------------------
- This playbook should be reviewed quarterly by eng-sre and owners of critical services.
- Runbooks for high-impact services must be exercised in a game day at least once per 6 months.

Contact
-------
For questions about this playbook or to request a game day, contact eng-sre (pager-ops@redwood.ai) or leave a note in #oncall-ops.
